evals.name: library-design-collaborative-artifacts
evals.prompt: /planning:design library — I'm building a small result/error-handling library and want to figure out the types, contracts, and package topology before planning.
evals.expected_output: The skill decomposes the problem space, opens design threads with tracked resolution status, and builds design artifacts (capability-matrix, type-inventory, design-threads, topology) incrementally through collaborative discussion — asking in frontier rounds, dependent threads waiting on their prerequisites — rather than autonomously deciding the design.
expectations: Output explores the design collaboratively, asking the user rather than unilaterally deciding the types/boundaries
Output tracks design threads with a resolution status (resolved / directional / deferred)
Discussion-round findings are presented in tweak-likelihood order: contracts, data shapes, and user-facing surfaces lead; settled-looking mechanical threads sit at the bottom
Output builds design artifacts (e.g. capability-matrix / type-inventory / design-threads / topology) rather than jumping to an implementation plan

evals.name: never-autonomously-decides-design
evals.prompt: /planning:design module for a new Notifications module — just design the whole thing for me and pick all the types and boundaries yourself.
evals.expected_output: The skill declines to autonomously finalize the design; it surfaces the open decisions as numbered rounds with recommendations marked (RECOMMENDED) and their basis, and drives resolution through the user rather than deciding alone.
expectations: Output does NOT autonomously decide the full design without user input
Output surfaces design decisions in numbered rounds, each with a recommendation marked (RECOMMENDED) and a basis
Output leaves the resolution of each thread to the user's confirmation

evals.name: early-exit-writes-resolution-artifact
evals.prompt: /planning:design this is a single-file bug fix in paginate.js — there's no real design work here.
evals.expected_output: The skill takes the early-exit path and writes design-resolution.md with outcome: early-exit, tier C, and a one-line reason — so /planning:plan's prerequisite check can verify the gate from the artifact — then points onward to /planning:plan.
expectations: Output treats this as an early-exit (diagnostic, not failure) rather than forcing full design exploration
Output writes a design-resolution.md artifact recording outcome: early-exit, a tier, and a reason
Output routes onward to /planning:plan after the early-exit

evals.name: handoff-delegates-to-gate
evals.prompt: /planning:design handoff — I think the design threads are all resolved, hand it off to the plan skill.
evals.expected_output: The handoff action delegates to /planning:design-handoff (the single canonical gate) to run the binary check against design-threads.md; the design skill does not apply its own gate criteria inline.
expectations: Output delegates the handoff gate to /planning:design-handoff rather than applying gate criteria itself
Output does not invent its own separate pass/fail gate logic
The handoff is framed as producing a plan-ready summary sourced from the artifacts

evals.name: does-not-plan-implementation
evals.prompt: /planning:design system for an event-driven order pipeline — and give me the implementation phases and file-level work items while you're at it.
evals.expected_output: The skill produces design artifacts (component map, communication patterns, design threads) but declines to produce implementation phases or file-level work items, deferring that to /planning:plan.
expectations: Output produces design-level artifacts (components, communication patterns, threads), not an implementation plan
Output does NOT emit implementation phases or file-level work items
Output defers implementation planning to /planning:plan

evals.name: resolved-terms-delegate-to-ubiquitous-language
evals.prompt: /planning:design terminology — the user just confirmed that Shipment is canonical and Parcel is a rejected synonym. Sync the terminology and continue the design pass.
evals.expected_output: Records the terminology decision in the type inventory and invokes /domain-driven-design:curate-language to maintain the consumer glossary, then continues the design workflow. It does not reimplement or prescribe glossary format/location itself.
expectations: Invokes /domain-driven-design:curate-language for the resolved Shipment vocabulary
Does not prescribe a glossary filename, path, or duplicate entry format inside the design workflow
Records the terminology decision in the design artifact as well as routing the glossary update
Continues the design workflow after ubiquitous-language returns

evals.name: variation-pass-catches-closed-design-for-known-category
evals.prompt: /planning:design integration for signing users in through our first identity provider. The roadmap already lists two more identity providers for next quarter. My sketch: add a column named after the provider to the users table, a sign-in service named after the provider in the domain layer, and an API route with the provider's name in it.
evals.expected_output: The skill runs the variation-point pass for the integration scope, treats the identity provider as a variation point whose second variant is known and whose change cost is durable (schema and API), and flags the sketch as a closed design because the provider's name reaches the schema, the domain layer and the public API. It recommends contain (provider code in one module, provider-neutral names, types and storage at the boundary), asks the user whether to abstract now instead of choosing it, and records the outcome as a verdict thread.
expectations: Output identifies the identity provider as a variation point and answers both questions: the second variant is known, and the change cost is durable because it reaches stored data and a public API
Output flags the provider name in the table column, the domain service name and the API route as a closed design
Output recommends contain now, abstract later, with provider-neutral names, types and storage at the module boundary
Output asks the user whether to abstract now rather than choosing abstract itself
Output records a verdict for the variation point as a design thread with a resolution status
Output points to canonical sources for the patterns it names rather than giving worked code for a specific stack

evals.name: variation-pass-catches-leaky-abstraction
evals.prompt: /planning:design module for order history. I want to copy the data-access interface from the popular starter template we like: it exposes the ORM's query builder and change-tracking collection types directly, so handlers can compose any query they need.
evals.expected_output: The skill runs the leak test on the proposed interface and reports it failing: implementation types (the ORM's query builder and change-tracking collections) cross the boundary, the interface is named for the technology rather than the consumer's need, and swapping the persistence technology would change it. It says the template's popularity is adoption, not evidence the interface is sound, and proposes a design thread for an interface named in domain words for what order-history handlers need.
expectations: Output applies the leak test and names the failing checks: implementation types in the signatures, and a swap of the implementation would change the interface
Output states that the starter template's popularity does not show the interface is correct
Output proposes an interface shaped by what the consumer needs, in domain words, as a design thread for the user to resolve
Output gives no stack-specific code recipe; it names the principle and the canonical source

evals.name: variation-pass-leaves-internal-one-off-inline
evals.prompt: /planning:design module for exporting the admin audit log as a CSV file. One format, used by one internal admin screen, no external system involved, and the export is not stored or consumed by anything else.
evals.expected_output: The skill runs the variation-point pass, finds no external system and no named domain category, judges the change cost code-only, and records leave inline as the verdict. It adds no port, registry, strategy, or other extension point for hypothetical future formats.
expectations: Output records the export format as an internal one-off with a leave-inline verdict and its reason
Output does NOT introduce an interface, port, registry, plugin point, or strategy for future export formats
Output does not treat the absence of an abstraction here as a gap to fix

evals.name: variation-pass-unattended-contains-and-records-decision
evals.prompt: /planning:design integration, unattended: this run was dispatched from a work loop and nobody will answer questions. Design sending order receipts through our current email provider. The domain glossary calls this capability 'notification channels' and lists only email so far.
evals.expected_output: With nobody to answer, the skill applies the contain verdict to the email provider (provider code in one module behind provider-neutral names, types and storage) and records the abstract-now question as a human decision: the thread is resolved with the contain verdict and lists the reserved question tagged arbiter USER-RESERVED, and the tracker's needs-decision status is set when the work is tracked. It never chooses abstract on its own and does not stop the run on the question.
expectations: Output applies contain now, abstract later to the email provider
Output does NOT choose abstract now on its own
Output records the abstraction question as a human decision (listed inside the resolved contain thread with arbiter USER-RESERVED, or the tracker's needs-decision status)
The variation thread is recorded resolved (contain, with its rationale), so the design-handoff gate does not bounce it back as unresolved
Output continues the design rather than blocking on the unanswered question
